There have been seasons when I questioned whether I fit anywhere clearly. I tried to narrow my calling into something easily defined. A title. A role. A description others could quickly understand. I wanted alignment that felt stable.

And yet the Lord kept pressing me toward something less tidy and more personal. I once wrote in my journal that I was not following a plan, but walking a path illuminated solely by Jesus. That path has often felt unconventional. At times misunderstood.

Comparison creeps in quietly. I see others with clear lanes and measurable outcomes. I wonder if my wiring is too strategic, too future-oriented, too different. When I attempt to conform, something in me grows restless.

The body of Christ does not need replicas. It needs surrendered distinctness. When believers live from who they were created to be, Christ becomes visible in fresh ways. True unity is not uniformity. It is Spirit-shaped uniqueness woven together in love. My task is not to fit someone else’s mold. It is to walk faithfully in the light given to me.
